newsitem.title: FRANCE: France criticises EU centrists' "no" to Turkey.
newsitem.headline: France criticises EU centrists' "no" to Turkey.

text.p: France distanced itself on Monday from a statement by European Christian Democratic and centrist leaders, including German Chancellor Helmut Kohl, that Turkey had no prospect of being admitted to the European Union.
In an interview with Reuters, French European Affairs Minister Michel Barnier said it was important not to slam the door on Turkey.

"I think it is important for the stability of the Union, that is to say for the stability of the whole of Europe, that the Turks retain a European prospect, even if we know that membership would not be realistic in the short-term," he said.

Barnier also warned Ankara's rulers against blocking the enlargement of NATO or of the EU to press their demands for accession to the 15-nation Union, as Turkish Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller has threatened to do.
"A country would have to think very carefully before taking hostage the enlargement of NATO or of the European Union to defend its own interests," the French minister said.
Meeting in Brussels last Tuesday, the leaders of Christian Democratic and centrist parties from Germany, Belgium, Italy, Luxembourg, Ireland and Spain rejected Turkey's EU candidacy.
The leader of the European People's Party, former Belgian prime minister Wilfried Martens, said bluntly: "Turkey is not a candidate to become a member of the European Union, short-term or long."
Barnier said: "That's one point of view, but it's not ours."
The issue may come to a head next weekend when EU foreign ministers meet at Appeldoorn in the Netherlands.
While no one sees Turkey joining the EU soon, French officials argue that overtly excluding Ankara could fuel Moslem fundamentalism and hostility towards the West.

That was one motive behind the EU's decision to conclude a customs union with Turkey in 1995, which was ratified despite Greek reluctance and opposition in the European Parliament over human rights and the Kurdish issue.
